loops.minute_1: Single snake (length 3) on empty grid; player learns 4-direction numpad control; first food eaten in ~5-10 seconds. Immediate growth feedback creates tight action→result loop. Zero cognitive load; causality is instant and obvious. Player thinks: 'Let me eat one more.'
loops.minute_10: Snake length 8-15; speed has increased 1-2 levels; space is noticeably constrained. Player must predict tail position 2-3 moves ahead. First close calls with self-collision occur. Difficulty ramps gradually (not spiking); frustration stays low. Spatial awareness becomes the challenge.
loops.hour_5: Snake length 40+; speed is 4-5 levels above baseline; grid is mostly occupied by player's own body. Each move is a spatial puzzle; sessions last 30-60 seconds once snake is large. Deep focus state; snake length (not speed alone) is the primary antagonist. Player is in extreme cognitive load.
loops.endgame: Death via self-collision or wall hit. Screen displays 'WASTED!' + score summary. Immediate restart available. No penalty, no progression loss (classic arcade model). Short session length (5-10 min typical) + clear measurable goal (highest score) = 'just one more' compelling.

games.retention_answer: Why does the player return? (1) Zero penalty on death—instant restart removes friction. (2) Clear score hierarchy—player sees improvement over time, creating intrinsic motivation. (3) Tight feedback loop—each action has immediate consequence. (4) Skill ladder visibility—outcome depends on player skill, not RNG.

sources.title: MDA – Slither.io – The Mechanics of Magic

loops.minute_1: Tiny snake spawns on crowded map with hundreds of other players visible. Immediate survival mode. Pellets scattered everywhere; first few eaten within seconds. Leaderboard visible showing top 10 snakes (some massive). Psychological effect: 'Wow, there's a LOT of players here.' Leaderboard visible at start creates immediate goal hierarchy. Player sees they are rank #2,847 out of thousands.
loops.minute_10: Snake length 20-50; player has climbed to rank #1,000 on server. Larger predators (length 100+) visible and lethal. Foraging vs. predation trade-off becomes visible. Boost mechanic enters play. Skill expression begins. Player learns boost is escape tool, not sustainable growth. Predator-prey dynamics emerge.
loops.hour_5: If player survives: snake length 200+, rank #10-50 globally. Map is dense with intense micro-wars. Every move is tactical. Player reads other snakes' patterns, predicts boost windows. Flow state achieved. PvP intensity is high. Player is fully engaged in predator-prey dynamics. Death is a reset, not a failure—it refuels the leaderboard climb.
loops.endgame: Collision with any snake's body (including own). Instant death animation. Corpse becomes food particles for others. Instant respawn at length 1 on same server. Session's rank is forgotten; leaderboard is real-time. 0-friction restart loop. Player chains sessions for hours because leaderboard is addictive feedback. Each session = micro-narrative: 'Am I better this run than last run?'

games.retention_answer: Why does the player return? (1) Leaderboard is addictive feedback—global rank visible creates urgency to climb. (2) PvP emergent dynamics—predator-prey tactics and greed cascades are fascinating to observe and execute. (3) Session-stateless design—no FOMO; no obligation to log in daily; high re-entry rate. (4) Skill ceiling is high—leaderboard winners are clearly skilled, not lucky or wealthy.

sources.title: Google Doodle Games Snake: A Timeless Digital Classic

loops.minute_1: Classic grid layout; single food; speed is slow (1 grid cell per ~200ms). Intuitive controls (arrow keys or swipe). First food consumed in ~5 seconds. Visual feedback is snappy; snake visibly grows. Accessibility is paramount. Rules are immediately intuitive. Player thinks: 'This is easy. I got this.'
loops.minute_10: Snake length 12-20; score 12-20; speed is still stable (no acceleration from Nokia-style speed scaling). Grid occupation is 15-20%. Spatial planning intensifies. Unlike Nokia (speed ramps), difficulty comes PURELY from snake length. Grid doesn't get faster; it just gets fuller. This distribution of difficulty is gentle and fair.
loops.hour_5: Snake length 60+; score 60+; grid occupation 30-40% (typical grid is 20×20). Almost every move requires precise timing. A single mistake (hitting self by 1 cell) ends the session. Extreme spatial mastery required. Player is in deep focus; no room for distraction. Sessions last 15-30 seconds once snake is large. High cognitive load.
loops.endgame: Self-collision or wall hit. Score summary displayed. Instant restart available. No penalty, no progression loss. Personal score is the only leaderboard. Players compete against own history. Personal mastery narrative: 'I can beat my PB of 47.' Short session length + clear measurable goal = re-entry friction is zero.

games.retention_answer: Why does the player return? (1) Personal score chase—player competes against own history, not against other players, avoiding social pressure. (2) Spatial mastery progression—clear skill progression; player sees improvement. (3) Gentle difficulty curve—speed doesn't ramp; space constraint ramps, giving player agency in difficulty. (4) Instant restart—zero friction to 'one more try.'
observable_mechanics: Power-ups (random spawns: Double Points, Slow-Motion, Invincibility)

common_patterns.significance: All three games make the snake unable to stop. This creates urgency and simplifies controls.
Player sees immediate visual consequence of action (food eaten = length increased). This is THE core reward loop.
Instant restart with no persistent loss (no grind loss, no cosmetic loss). This is why players accept repeated failure.
Outcome depends on player skill, not RNG or spending. This creates intrinsic motivation.
Snake's own body is the main antagonist. This is elegant: no external threat, just self-vs-self resource optimization.

retention_mechanisms: Tight action→result feedback loop (causality is instant)
Zero pressure to spend (all fully playable free-to-play)
Short session length (5-10 min typical; low commitment barrier)
economy_consistency: All three are cosmetic-monetized or free (no gameplay pay-to-win)
Score/rank is the only persistent metric
No grind, no daily quests, no sunk-cost loops
Accessibility is paramount: everyone plays under same rules
